summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with altered mental status and weakness following a fall, in the context of relapsed multiple myeloma. His confusion was attributed to hypercalcemia (calcium 10.7), which improved with IV fluids and pamidronate. He had an elevated creatinine of 1.7, consistent with acute kidney injury likely due to dehydration and hypercalcemia, which resolved with treatment. A single blood culture grew coagulase-negative staph, but it was deemed a contaminant given no fever and negative repeat cultures; IV vancomycin was discontinued. His multiple myeloma remained active, and he missed a scheduled daratumumab dose, which was rescheduled post-discharge. He was managed for diabetes with insulin, continued lamivudine for hepatitis B, and treated for constipation with stool softeners. His mental status normalized, and he was discharged home with services in stable condition.
